title: Feasibility Study on the Integration of AR-based Entertainment and Distraction for Isolated Patients with Uveal Melanoma
summary:
Patients with uveal melanoma undergoing brachytherapy are required by law to remain in isolation in a radiation-protected area of the hospital for several days. This isolation is often associated with loneliness, boredom, and psychological distress.
This study investigates whether a lightweight augmented reality (AR) video headset can provide a practical and acceptable means of entertainment, distraction, and relaxation in this situation. The AR glasses project a virtual large screen into the user's field of view, allowing patients to watch films, series, or other content via their own smartphone or tablet – discreetly, comfortably, and without disturbing others in the room.
The aim of the study is to assess whether patients accept the use of the glasses, whether they find them pleasant and helpful, and whether their use is feasible in everyday clinical practice. The findings are intended to help improve the well-being of patients in isolation settings in the future.

interventions.name:
A monocentric, exploratory feasibility study without randomization or blinding.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient brachytherapy with radiation protection-related isolation
Capacity to provide informed consent
Sufficient German language skills (written and spoken)
Availability of a compatible personal mobile device (smartphone, tablet, or notebook with USB-C port with DisplayPort functionality or Lightning connector)
Written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Neurological conditions precluding safe use of the AR glasses (e.g., photosensitive epilepsy, dementia, delirium/transitional syndrome)
Severe psychiatric disorders (e.g., schizophrenia)
Strong susceptibility to nausea (e.g., motion sickness) or known balance disorders
